title: Decelerating an interstellar probe at its destination
bottleneck: Every credible interstellar propulsion scheme — beamed sails, fusion rockets, antimatter — is optimized for accelerating away from the Sun, but a flyby probe crosses its target star system in days, far too fast for meaningful science. Slowing from a fraction of light speed needs as much energy as speeding up, and there is no destination infrastructure to help: no laser array, no fuel depot, no atmosphere for aerobraking. Staged sails, magnetic sails braking on the interstellar medium, and onboard photon rockets all demand technologies that do not exist.
why_it_blocks: Without deceleration, interstellar missions collect days of data after decades of travel — a catastrophic return on investment that undermines the scientific case for going at all.
current_state: Forward's staged-sail concept and magnetic-sail braking remain theoretical. Starshot explicitly accepts a flyby; no funded program is developing interstellar deceleration.
